content.question: What is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, where air density is highest and important atmospheric processes like climate and weather occur?
content.note:
The Troposphere is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere.
It contains roughly 80% of the atmosphere's mass and 99% of its water vapor.
Note: This is the only layer where weather (clouds, rain, storms) occurs because of the high air density and convective activity.

content.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
content.note:
Gujarat has the longest coastline in India, stretching over 1,600 km.
Its indented nature and presence of the Gulf of Khambhat and Gulf of Kutch contribute to its length.
Note: Andhra Pradesh has the second-longest coastline in India.

content.question: The Northern Plains of India are made up of which type of soil?
content.note:
The Northern Plains are formed by the interplay of three major river systems: the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra.
These rivers deposit Alluvial Soil, which is extremely fertile and rich in potash.
Note: This region is the 'granary of India' due to its high agricultural productivity.

content.question: Tea and coffee are grown in which type of soil?
content.note:
Laterite soil is ideal for plantation crops like tea, coffee, and cashew nuts.
It develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall, leading to intense leaching.
Note: It is rich in iron oxide (giving it a red color) but poor in nitrogen and lime.

content.question: What is the longest/largest river of Peninsular India that flows into the Bay of Bengal?
content.note:
The Godavari is the largest peninsular river, often referred to as the 'Dakshina Ganga'.
It rises in the Nashik district of Maharashtra and empties into the Bay of Bengal. Related info: Its catchment area covers parts of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.

content.question: The Indira Gandhi Canal, India's longest irrigation canal project, is located on which river?
content.note:
The Indira Gandhi Canal draws its water from the Harike Barrage at the confluence of the Sutlej and Beas rivers.
It transformed the Thar Desert into a green belt.
Note: It is one of the largest canal projects in the world, primarily serving Rajasthan.

content.question: Which country is the largest producer of Uranium in the world?
content.note:
Kazakhstan is the world's leading producer of Uranium, accounting for over 40% of global supply.
It has vast natural reserves and advanced mining infrastructure. Other options: Canada and Australia are also major producers, but Kazakhstan has held the top spot since 2009.

content.question: Name the strait that separates India from Sri Lanka.
content.note:
The Palk Strait is a narrow stretch of water between the Tamil Nadu state of India and the Jaffna District of Sri Lanka.
It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with Palk Bay in the southwest.
Note: It is named after Robert Palk, a former Governor of Madras Presidency.

content.question: The mainland of India lies between which latitudes?
content.note:
The mainland of India extends between latitudes 8°4' N and 37°6' N.
This places India entirely in the Northern Hemisphere. Related info: The Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes almost halfway through the country.

content.question: India's first national park, established in 1936, was named what?
content.answer: Hailey National Park (now known as Jim Corbett National Park, Uttarakhand).
content.note:
Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, it is now known as Jim Corbett National Park.
It was the first park to come under the Project Tiger initiative.
Note: It is located in the Nainital district of Uttarakhand and is famous for its Royal Bengal Tigers.

content.question: Which is the brightest and hottest planet in our solar system, also known as the 'Morning and Evening Star'?
content.note:
Venus is the hottest planet (due to a thick CO2 atmosphere causing a runaway greenhouse effect) and the brightest.
It is visible just before sunrise or after sunset, earning it the nicknames Morning Star and Evening Star.
Note: It is the second planet from the Sun.

content.question: The microorganisms or organic matter present in the soil are collectively called what?
content.note:
Humus is the dark, organic material in soil produced by the decomposition of plant and animal matter by microorganisms.
It is essential for soil fertility as it provides nutrients and helps retain moisture.
Note: A high humus content gives soil a dark, crumbly texture.

content.question: Manas National Park and Kaziranga National Park are located in which state?
content.note:
Both Manas and Kaziranga are located in Assam.
They are UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Difference: Kaziranga is famous for the one-horned rhino, while Manas is known for its tiger reserve and rare biosphere including the Pygmy Hog.

content.question: Which meridian determines Indian Standard Time (IST)?
content.note:
Indian Standard Time is calculated based on the 82.5° E (82°30'E) longitude.
This meridian passes through Mirzapur (near Prayagraj) in Uttar Pradesh.
Note: IST is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).

content.question: In which state/union territory is the natural habitat of the one-horned rhinoceros (Indian rhino) located?
content.note:
The One-horned Rhinoceros is primarily found in the wetlands of Assam, specifically in Kaziranga National Park.
Over 90% of the world's population of this species lives here.
Note: It is listed as 'Vulnerable' on the IUCN Red List.

content.question: In a region, interacting biotic components together with the non-living (abiotic) components of the environment form what?
content.note:
An Ecosystem consists of Biotic (living) and Abiotic (non-living) components interacting as a system.
These components are linked together through nutrient cycles and energy flows. Example: A pond, a forest, or even a small garden can be an ecosystem.

content.question: The saturated underground layer that helps supply water to a well at a sufficient rate is called what?
content.note:
An Aquifer is a body of porous rock or sediment saturated with groundwater.
Groundwater enters an aquifer as precipitation seeps through the soil.
Note: It serves as a vital source of water for drinking and irrigation via wells.

content.question: Where is the highest biodiversity found?
content.note:
Tropical Rainforests harbor the highest biodiversity on Earth.
The warm, rainy climate supports year-round plant growth, creating complex habitats for millions of species. Fact: They cover less than 7% of Earth's land but house more than half of its plant and animal species.

content.question: Which is the largest tropical rainforest in the world?
content.note:
The Amazon Rainforest in South America is the world's largest tropical rainforest.
It spans nine nations and is often called the 'Lungs of the Planet' for its role in oxygen production and carbon sequestration.
Note: It is home to the Amazon River, the largest river by discharge.

content.question: Which is the largest pulse-producing state in India?
content.note:
Madhya Pradesh is the leading producer of pulses in India.
The state's climate and soil are well-suited for crops like gram, tur (arhar), and urad.
Note: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses.

content.question: Which type of soil develops over crystalline igneous rocks in low rainfall areas of the eastern and southern parts of the Deccan Plateau?
content.note:
Red Soil occupies the largest area in the Deccan Plateau after Black soil.
It gets its color from the presence of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks.
Note: It becomes yellow when it occurs in a hydrated form.

content.question: In which crop season are watermelon, muskmelon, etc., grown in India?
content.note:
Zaid is a short season between the Rabi (winter) and Kharif (monsoon) seasons, usually from March to June.
It is the season for summer crops like watermelon, cucumber, and fodder crops. Related info: These crops require warm, dry weather for growth and a longer day length for flowering.

content.question: What is the largest reservoir of fresh water?
content.note:
Glaciers and ice caps hold about 68.7% of the world's fresh water.
Although oceans are larger, they contain saltwater.
Note: After glaciers, groundwater is the next largest reservoir of fresh water.

content.question: Which planet in our solar system is similar in size to Earth and is also known as the 'Earth's twin sister'?
content.note:
Venus is often called Earth's Twin.
It is very similar to Earth in terms of size, mass, density, and composition. Difference: Despite the physical similarities, its atmosphere is toxic and its surface temperature is hot enough to melt lead.

content.question: Where do the Western and Eastern Ghats meet each other?
content.note:
The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills (Blue Mountains).
This junction point is located in the tri-junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka.
Note: Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiris.

content.question: The technique of watering plants through narrow pipes, delivering water directly to their roots, is called what?
content.note:
Drip Irrigation (or Trickle Irrigation) delivers water slowly to the base of the plant.
It minimizes evaporation and runoff, making it highly water-efficient.
Note: It is particularly useful in arid regions and for high-value orchard crops.

content.question: The bowl-shaped or cup-like depressions that contain volcanic remnants are called what?
content.note:
A Crater is a circular depression in the ground caused by volcanic activity.
It is typically a bowl-shaped feature where the vent is located. Related info: If a crater becomes very large (usually due to a collapse), it is called a Caldera.

content.question: Gahirmatha Sanctuary in Odisha is the only sanctuary in the state for which animal?
content.note:
Gahirmatha is famous for being the world's largest nesting beach for Olive Ridley Turtles.
Thousands of turtles arrive here every year for Arribada (mass nesting). Location: It is located in the Kendrapara district of Odisha.

content.question: Which mountain is called the 'Young Fold Mountains'?
content.note:
The Himalayas are called Young Fold Mountains because they were formed only 40 to 50 million years ago.
Compared to the Aravalis (which are old fold mountains), the Himalayas are still growing as the tectonic plates continue to push against each other.
Note: They are characterized by high peaks and deep valleys.

content.question: The Eld's deer subspecies, classified as endangered on the IUCN Red List, is found only in which National Park in Manipur?
content.note:
The Eld's Deer (also known as the Sangai or dancing deer) is found only at Keibul Lamjao National Park.
This is the world's only floating national park, located on Loktak Lake. Status: It is the state animal of Manipur.
